slides.title: A 26-year-old primigravida client at 4 weeks gestation arrives at the outpatient
text:
Question: A 26-year-old primigravida client at 4 weeks gestation arrives at the outpatient clinic for an initial prenatal visit.
Which of the following should the nurse address first?
A. Encourage the client to schedule a tour of the birth facility.
B. Describe the expected weight gain pattern for the client.
C. Acknowledge the client’s feelings about pregnancy.
D. Review the signs of imminent labor with the client.
Correct answer: C. Acknowledge the client’s feelings about pregnancy.
Topic: Maternal-Newborn
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Acknowledge the client’s feelings about pregnancy.
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Acknowledge the client’s feelings about pregnancy.” – Assess early pregnancy adjustment
Not correct:
• “Encourage the client to schedule a tour of the birth facility.” – Can be addressed later
• “Describe the expected weight gain pattern for the client.” – Nutrition teaching follows initial concerns
• “Review the signs of imminent labor with the client.” – Labor teaching is premature
Not covered in your class PowerPoints, so this answer comes from the quiz file only.
Also appears in the weekly quiz for: Unit 5 (B), Unit 5 (C).

slides.title: The nurse is caring for a newborn infant who was born 1 hour ago and is resting
text:
Question: The nurse is caring for a newborn infant who was born 1 hour ago and is resting quietly in the mother’s arms. Maintains head position in direction of mother’s voice. Vital signs: 97.7°F (36.5°C), apical P 158, RR 52. Occasional nasal flaring observed, coarse lung sounds per auscultation, and acrocyanosis to the feet. Mucus membranes and nailbeds are pink.
Complete the following sentence with one of the following options.
The nurse should first attend to __________.
A. Feeding tolerance.
B. Coarse lung sounds.
C. Apical pulse.
D. Feet discoloration.
Correct answer: A. Feeding tolerance.
Topic: Maternal-Newborn
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Feeding tolerance.
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Feeding tolerance.” – Source prioritizes coordinated sucking and breathing; assess persistent distress
Not correct:
• “Coarse lung sounds.” – May reflect transitional fluid; persistent abnormal sounds need assessment
• “Apical pulse.” – 158 is within newborn range
• “Feet discoloration.” – Acrocyanosis may be normal initially
Not covered in your class PowerPoints, so this answer comes from the quiz file only.
Also appears in the weekly quiz for: Unit 5 (B), Unit 5 (C).

slides.title: A nurse is caring for a hospitalized child who is receiving a continuous infusio
text: Question: A nurse is caring for a hospitalized child who is receiving a continuous infusion of intravenous (IV) potassium for the treatment of dehydration. The nurse monitors the child closely and notifies the physician if which of the following is noted?
A. Blood pressure (BP) unchanged from baseline
B. A decrease in urine output to 0.5 mL/kg/hr
C. Temperature of 100.8º F rectally
D. Weight increase of 0.5 kg
Correct answer: B. A decrease in urine output to 0.5 mL/kg/hr
Topic: Pediatrics
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• A decrease in urine output to 0.5 mL/kg/hr
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “A decrease in urine output to 0.5 mL/kg/hr” – Low output risks potassium retention
Not correct:
• “Blood pressure (BP) unchanged from baseline” – No new BP change
• “Temperature of 100.8º F rectally” – Requires assessment but not potassium-specific
• “Weight increase of 0.5 kg” – Assess trend; output is more directly relevant
Not covered in your class PowerPoints, so this answer comes from the quiz file only.

slides.title: What do parents of preschool children need to understand about discipline?
text: Question: What do parents of preschool children need to understand about discipline?
A. The method of discipline should be consistent with that of the child’s peers.
B. Discipline should include positive reinforcement of desired behaviors.
C. Discipline should involve some physical restriction.
D. Both parents and the child should agree on the method of discipline.
Correct answer: B. Discipline should include positive reinforcement of desired behaviors.
Topic: Pediatrics
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Discipline should include positive reinforcement of desired behaviors.
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Discipline should include positive reinforcement of desired behaviors.” – Reinforces desirable behavior
Not correct:
• “The method of discipline should be consistent with that of the child’s peers.” – Tailor discipline to child and family
• “Discipline should involve some physical restriction.” – Physical restriction is not routine discipline
• “Both parents and the child should agree on the method of discipline.” – Parents set consistent limits
Not covered in your class PowerPoints, so this answer comes from the quiz file only.

slides.title: The nurse teaches parents signs that a child might be being bullied or otherwise
text: Question: The nurse teaches parents signs that a child might be being bullied or otherwise victimized. What signs does the nurse include in this teaching? (Select all that apply.)
A. The child wants to be driven to school.
B. School performance improves.
C. Belongings frequently go missing or are damaged.
D. The child freely talks about his day.
E. Spends an inordinate amount of time in the nurse’s office
Correct answers: A. The child wants to be driven to school.; C. Belongings frequently go missing or are damaged.; E. Spends an inordinate amount of time in the nurse’s office
Topic: Pediatrics
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (select all):
• The child wants to be driven to school.
• Belongings frequently go missing or are damaged.
• Spends an inordinate amount of time in the nurse’s office
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “The child wants to be driven to school.” – Avoiding the trip may signal bullying
• “Belongings frequently go missing or are damaged.” – Lost or damaged items can signal bullying
• “Spends an inordinate amount of time in the nurse’s office” – Frequent somatic complaints may reflect bullying
Not correct:
• “School performance improves.” – Improvement is not a typical warning sign
• “The child freely talks about his day.” – Open communication is reassuring
Not covered in your class PowerPoints, so this answer comes from the quiz file only.

slides.title: A patient is being admitted to prenatal care by the nurse. The patient states he
text: Question: A patient is being admitted to prenatal care by the nurse. The patient states her last menstrual period was October 30, 2018. The nurse correctly calculates this mother’s due date as (select an answer from the following options):
B. August 6, 2019
D. August 13, 2019
Correct answer: B. August 6, 2019
Topic: Maternal-Newborn
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• August 6, 2019
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “August 6, 2019” – Naegele rule: October 30 plus 7 days minus 3 months plus 1 year
Not correct:
• “July 30, 2019” – Omits seven-day addition
• “July 23, 2019” – Subtracts rather than adds days
• “August 13, 2019” – Adds an extra week
Not covered in your class PowerPoints, so this answer comes from the quiz file only.

slides.title: A pregnant client calls the nurse at the physician’s office and reports that she
text: Question: A pregnant client calls the nurse at the physician’s office and reports that she has noticed a thin, colorless, vaginal drainage. Which of the following information would be most appropriate for the nurse to provide to the client?
A. Use tampons if the discharge is bothersome but be sure to change the tampons every 2 hours.
B. Report to the emergency department at the maternity center immediately.
C. Come to the clinic immediately.
D. The vaginal discharge may be bothersome but is a normal occurrence.
Correct answer: D. The vaginal discharge may be bothersome but is a normal occurrence.
Topic: Maternal-Newborn
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• The vaginal discharge may be bothersome but is a normal occurrence.
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “The vaginal discharge may be bothersome but is a normal occurrence.” – Normal discharge is possible; watery leakage warrants assessment
Not correct:
• “Use tampons if the discharge is bothersome but be sure to change the tampons every 2 ho…” – Tampons are not recommended
• “Report to the emergency department at the maternity center immediately.” – Not routine for benign leukorrhea; suspected fluid leak needs evaluation
• “Come to the clinic immediately.” – Urgency depends on possible membrane rupture
Not covered in your class PowerPoints, so this answer comes from the quiz file only.

slides.title: A nurse is counseling a newly pregnant woman with borderline high blood pressure
text: Question: A nurse is counseling a newly pregnant woman with borderline high blood pressure readings about symptoms to contact the clinic during the pregnancy related to preeclampsia. The nurse correctly tells the patient to call immediately if (select an answer from the following options):
A. The patient has ankle edema at the end of the day.
B. Her weight increases by 2 lbs. in a week or 5 lbs. in four weeks.
C. There is any wrist pain with numbness on the sides of the fingers.
D. She experiences any significant headaches, visual changes or epigastric pain.
Correct answer: D. She experiences any significant headaches, visual changes or epigastric pain.
Topic: Maternal-Newborn
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• She experiences any significant headaches, visual changes or epigastric pain.
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “She experiences any significant headaches, visual changes or epigastric pain.” – Severe preeclampsia warning symptoms
Not correct:
• “The patient has ankle edema at the end of the day.” – Dependent edema can be normal
• “Her weight increases by 2 lbs. in a week or 5 lbs. in four weeks.” – Not the listed severe-feature cluster
• “There is any wrist pain with numbness on the sides of the fingers.” – Suggests carpal tunnel
Not covered in your class PowerPoints, so this answer comes from the quiz file only.

slides.title: The nurse is evaluating a patient who states her last period was approximately 8
text: Question: The nurse is evaluating a patient who states her last period was approximately 8 weeks ago. The patient relates symptoms of morning nausea, breast tenderness, and a positive pregnancy test. The patient further states all symptoms have subsided in the last week with scant pink vaginal discharge. The nurse correctly suspects that this patient (select an answer from the following options):
A. was not really pregnant
B. has a possible eating disorder
C. is experiencing a spontaneous abortion
D. is presenting with a hormonal imbalance
Correct answer: C. is experiencing a spontaneous abortion
Topic: Maternal-Newborn
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• is experiencing a spontaneous abortion
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “is experiencing a spontaneous abortion” – Possible pregnancy loss; evaluate urgently as appropriate
Not correct:
• “was not really pregnant” – Positive test supports pregnancy
• “has a possible eating disorder” – Does not explain bleeding and symptom loss
• “is presenting with a hormonal imbalance” – Less specific than pregnancy loss
✔ Checked against your PowerPoints:
• Unit 5 - OB and Newborn Care, slide 23: “Abortion”

slides.title: A patient presents to the clinic for her first prenatal appointment. She states
text: Question: A patient presents to the clinic for her first prenatal appointment. She states that she has had a set of twins who were born at 34 weeks, a son who was born at 40 weeks, and she has had two miscarriages.
Correct answer: C. 5-1-1-2-3
Topic: Maternal-Newborn
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “5-1-1-2-3” – Five pregnancies, one term, one preterm, two losses, three living
Not correct:
• “5-1-2-2-3” – Twins count as one preterm pregnancy
• “5-1-2-2-3” – Same incorrect preterm count
• “6-1-1-2-3” – Overcounts pregnancies
✔ Checked against your PowerPoints:
• Unit 5 - OB and Newborn Care, slide 8: “Para: births after 20 weeks gestation”
• Unit 5 - OB and Newborn Care, slide 8: “Abortions: birth that occurs <20 weeks gestation”
Worked out with your slide definitions: gravida 5 (with this pregnancy), term 1, preterm 1 (twins at 34 weeks), abortions 2, living 3.

text: Question: A patient presents to the clinic for her first prenatal appointment. She states that she has one child living who was born at 35 weeks gestation. Which of the following would be her correct GPTPtAL?
Correct answer: D. 2-1-0-1-0-1
Topic: Maternal-Newborn
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “2-1-0-1-0-1” – Two pregnancies, one para, zero term, one preterm, zero losses, one living
Not correct:
• “1-1-0-1-0-1” – Omits current pregnancy

• “1-1-1-0-0-1” – Omits current pregnancy and misclassifies birth

slides.title: The nurse has developed a plan of care for a client experiencing dystocia and in
text: Question: The nurse has developed a plan of care for a client experiencing dystocia and includes several nursing interventions in the plan. The nurse prioritizes the plan and selects which of the following nursing interventions as the highest priority?
A. Keeping the significant other informed of the progress of the labor
B. Changing the client’s position frequently
C. Providing comfort measures
D. Monitoring fetal status
Correct answer: D. Monitoring fetal status
Topic: Maternal-Newborn
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Monitoring fetal status
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Monitoring fetal status” – Dystocia risks fetal compromise
Not correct:
• “Keeping the significant other informed of the progress of the labor” – Supportive but not immediate fetal priority
• “Changing the client’s position frequently” – May help labor but fetal assessment first
• “Providing comfort measures” – Comfort secondary to fetal safety
Not covered in your class PowerPoints, so this answer comes from the quiz file only.
Also appears in the weekly quiz for: Unit 5 (C).

slides.title: The nurse caring for a woman in active labor notes late decelerations in the fet
text: Question: The nurse caring for a woman in active labor notes late decelerations in the fetal heart tones. The first action of the nurse would be to:
A. Reposition the woman.
B. Readjust the external monitor.
C. Call the primary caregiver.
D. Start oxygen by mask.
Correct answer: A. Reposition the woman.
Topic: Maternal-Newborn
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Reposition the woman.
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Reposition the woman.” – Improves uteroplacental perfusion
Not correct:
• “Readjust the external monitor.” – Does not correct uteroplacental insufficiency
• “Call the primary caregiver.” – Notify after immediate corrective measures as appropriate
• “Start oxygen by mask.” – Not routine if maternal saturation normal
✔ Checked against your PowerPoints:
• Unit 5 - OB and Newborn Care, slide 78: “Position mother on left side”
• Unit 5 - OB and Newborn Care, slide 78: “Provide O2 to mother”
Your slide lists repositioning and oxygen among the interventions; it does not rank which comes first.

slides.title: Which CHD results in increased pulmonary blood flow?
text: Question: Which CHD results in increased pulmonary blood flow?
A. Ventricular septal defect
B. Pulmonary stenosis
C. Tetralogy of Fallot
D. Coarctation of the aorta
Correct answer: A. Ventricular septal defect
Topic: Pediatrics
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Ventricular septal defect
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Ventricular septal defect” – Left-to-right shunt increases pulmonary flow
Not correct:
• “Pulmonary stenosis” – Obstructs pulmonary outflow
• “Tetralogy of Fallot” – Typically decreases pulmonary flow
• “Coarctation of the aorta” – Obstructs systemic outflow
✔ Checked against your PowerPoints:
• Unit 5 - Pediatrics, slide 27: “Disorders with increased pulmonary blood flow (Acyanotic)”

slides.title: A nurse is conducting discharge teaching to parents about the care of their infa
text: Question: A nurse is conducting discharge teaching to parents about the care of their infant after cardiac surgery. The nurse instructs the parents to notify the physician if which conditions occur? (Select all that apply.)
A. Respiratory rate of 36 at rest
B. Temperature above 37.7° C (100° F)
C. New, frequent coughing
D. Turning blue or bluer than normal
E. Appetite slowly increasing
Correct answers: B. Temperature above 37.7° C (100° F); C. New, frequent coughing; D. Turning blue or bluer than normal
Topic: Pediatrics
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (select all):
• Temperature above 37.7° C (100° F)
• New, frequent coughing
• Turning blue or bluer than normal
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Temperature above 37.7° C (100° F)” – Fever may indicate infection
• “New, frequent coughing” – New cough may indicate respiratory compromise
• “Turning blue or bluer than normal” – Worsening cyanosis indicates poor oxygenation
Not correct:
• “Respiratory rate of 36 at rest” – May be normal for infant at rest
• “Appetite slowly increasing” – Improving appetite is reassuring
Not covered in your class PowerPoints, so this answer comes from the quiz file only.
Also appears in the weekly quiz for: Unit 5 (B).

slides.title: Exophthalmos (protruding eyeballs) may occur in children with which condition?
text: Question: Exophthalmos (protruding eyeballs) may occur in children with which condition?
A. Hypoparathyroidism
B. Hypothyroidism
C. Hyperparathyroidism
D. Hyperthyroidism
Correct answer: D. Hyperthyroidism
Topic: Endocrine & Metabolic
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Hyperthyroidism
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Hyperthyroidism” – Excess thyroid hormone increases metabolism
Not correct:
• “Hypoparathyroidism” – Usually causes low calcium
• “Hypothyroidism” – Slows metabolism
• “Hyperparathyroidism” – Usually causes high calcium
Not covered in your class PowerPoints, so this answer comes from the quiz file only.
Also appears in the weekly quiz for: Unit 5 (B), Unit 9.

slides.title: A nurse is assessing lab results on four patients in the general pediatric unit.
text: Question: A nurse is assessing lab results on four patients in the general pediatric unit. What child should the nurse go see first?
A. Urine ketones: positive in large amounts
B. Serum creatinine 0.7 mg/dL
C. Serum BUN 21 mg/dL
D. Urine specific gravity: 1.025
Correct answer: A. Urine ketones: positive in large amounts
Topic: Pediatrics
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Urine ketones: positive in large amounts
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Urine ketones: positive in large amounts” – Large ketones suggest ketosis and possible DKA
Not correct:
• “Serum creatinine 0.7 mg/dL” – Generally normal creatinine
• “Serum BUN 21 mg/dL” – Mild elevation is less specific
• “Urine specific gravity: 1.025” – Concentration is less specific than ketonuria
Not covered in your class PowerPoints, so this answer comes from the quiz file only.

slides.title: Which nursing diagnosis has the highest priority for the toddler with celiac dis
text: Question: Which nursing diagnosis has the highest priority for the toddler with celiac disease?
A. Risk for Disproportionate Growth related to obesity
B. Excess Fluid Volume related to celiac crisis
C. Disturbed Body Image related to chronic constipation
D. Imbalanced Nutrition: Less than Body Requirements related to malabsorption
Correct answer: D. Imbalanced Nutrition: Less than Body Requirements related to malabsorption
Topic: GI & Nutrition
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Imbalanced Nutrition: Less than Body Requirements related to malabsorption
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Imbalanced Nutrition: Less than Body Requirements related to malabsorption” – Poor absorption causes inadequate nutrient uptake
Not correct:
• “Risk for Disproportionate Growth related to obesity” – Malabsorption generally impairs growth
• “Excess Fluid Volume related to celiac crisis” – Dehydration can occur in crisis
• “Disturbed Body Image related to chronic constipation” – Does not address primary nutrition issue
Not covered in your class PowerPoints, so this answer comes from the quiz file only.

slides.title: A school-age child with diarrhea has been rehydrated. The nurse is discussing th
text: Question: A school-age child with diarrhea has been rehydrated. The nurse is discussing the child’s diet with the family. Which statement by the parent indicates a correct understanding of the teaching?
A. “I will keep my child on a clear liquid diet for the next 24 hours.”
B. “I will offer my child bananas, rice, applesauce, and toast for the next 48 hours.”
C. “I should have my child eat a normal diet with easily digested foods for the next 48 hours.”
D. “I should encourage my child to drink carbonated drinks but avoid food for the next 24 hours.”
Correct answer: C. “I should have my child eat a normal diet with easily digested foods for the next 48 hours.”
Topic: GI & Nutrition
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• “I should have my child eat a normal diet with easily digested foods for the next 48 hours.”
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• ““I should have my child eat a normal diet with easily digested foods for the next 48 ho…” – Resume age-appropriate foods after rehydration
Not correct:
• ““I will keep my child on a clear liquid diet for the next 24 hours.”” – Prolonged restriction delays nutrition
• ““I will offer my child bananas, rice, applesauce, and toast for the next 48 hours.”” – BRAT diet lacks needed nutrients
• ““I should encourage my child to drink carbonated drinks but avoid food for the next 24 …” – Carbonation and fasting are not recommended
Not covered in your class PowerPoints, so this answer comes from the quiz file only.
Also appears in the weekly quiz for: Unit 7.

slides.title: In caring for a child with an open fracture, the nurse should carefully assess f
text: Question: In caring for a child with an open fracture, the nurse should carefully assess for
A. infection.
B. osteoarthritis.
C. epiphyseal disruption.
D. periosteum thickening.
Correct answer: A. infection.
Topic: Neuro, Eyes & Ortho
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• infection.
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “infection.” – Open fracture allows microorganisms to enter
Not correct:
• “osteoarthritis.” – Degenerative joint disease is not the immediate open-fracture concern
• “epiphyseal disruption.” – Growth plate injury is possible but infection is the immediate open-fracture concern
• “periosteum thickening.” – Not the primary complication of an open fracture

slides.title: When infants are seen for fractures, which nursing intervention is a priority?
text: Question: When infants are seen for fractures, which nursing intervention is a priority?
A. Assess for child abuse. Fractures in infants are often nonaccidental.
B. Assess for genetic factors.
C. No intervention is necessary. It is not uncommon for infants to fracture bones.
D. Assess the family’s safety practices. Fractures in infants usually result from falls.
Correct answer: A. Assess for child abuse. Fractures in infants are often nonaccidental.
Topic: Pediatrics
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Assess for child abuse. Fractures in infants are often nonaccidental.
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Assess for child abuse. Fractures in infants are often nonaccidental.” – Unexplained infant fracture requires safeguarding evaluation
Not correct:
• “Assess for genetic factors.” – Consider bone disease but do not bypass abuse evaluation
• “No intervention is necessary. It is not uncommon for infants to fracture bones.” – Fractures are not routine in infants
• “Assess the family’s safety practices. Fractures in infants usually result from falls.” – Falls do not explain all infant fractures
Not covered in your class PowerPoints, so this answer comes from the quiz file only.
